newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Airline estimates are lowered.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Airline estimates are lowered.

text.p: CS First Boston said Tuesday it had lowered its 1997 earnings estimates for several airline companies. It said it expects weak second quarter results because of fare sales.
-- Analyst Tom Schreier said he lowered his full-year 1997 estimate on Delta Air Lines Inc to $11.78 per share from $12.23, and cut his second quarter estimate to $4.14 from $4.58.

-- "From the domestic perspective, we expect second quarter weakness across the sector," he said. "We attribute the weakness to a fare sale by Delta which is over now but which put too much inventory on sale at too low a price."
-- Schreier said industry sales generated air traffic at the expense of revenue yield.
-- He said he lowered his 1997 earnings estimate on AMR Corp to $9.50 per share from $9.77, and cut his second quarter estimate to $3.20 from $3.41.
-- For Northwest Airlines Corp, Schreier cut his 1997 estimate to $4.68 per share from $5.52, and cut his second quarter estimate to $1.07 from $1.58.

-- "In addition to domestic weakness, the Pacific region is weak and Northwest has high Japan-exposure," he said. "Japan traffic is tough and the company also made an ill-timed yen hedge which will cost it about $30 million in the second quarter."
